subject: Avalon Health - AZ2 throughput burst causing 502s / expedited routing
messages:
From: Mike O'Neil <ops@avalonhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-lead@avalonhealth.com (Sofia Park)
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: High 502 spike and dropped throughput in us-west-2 (AZ2)

Rafael —

We're seeing a sustained spike of 502s and a 60% drop in checkout throughput originating from AZ2 (us-west-2a) starting ~07:50 PDT this morning. This is impacting our payment flow; conversion has dropped by ~40% and we've had multiple payment errors. Can you confirm whether this is a routing / capacity issue on Redwood's side or something specific to our integration?

Attached is a short Kibana snapshot and sample request ids. We need urgent mitigation and an ETA for a fix or a recommended work-around (cross-region drain/redirect).

Mike
Ops, Avalon Health
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Mike O'Neil <ops@avalonhealth.com>, eng-lead@avalonhealth.com (Sofia Park)
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 502 spike and dropped throughput in us-west-2 (AZ2)

Mike —

Thanks for the heads up and the Kibana snapshot. I'm opening a P0 on our side and looping in Vanessa (on-call routing lead) and Hannah (ops leadership) for exec visibility. Initial triage: we see elevated 502 ratios from AZ2 paired with KV-cache saturation on the serving tier for your tenant; throughput for long-running streaming sessions dropped which likely explains the checkout retries.

Immediate next steps we recommend (short window mitigation):
- Start a controlled traffic divert to us-west-2-b and eu-west-1 for checkout routes (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% if healthy)
- Apply temporary request-level retry policy (disable aggressive client retries for 30m)
- Provision an emergency burst pool for Avalon to relieve KV cache hot shards (we can spin up reserved nodes in 10–12 minutes)

I'll share a short evacuation plan (traffic-metrics + proposed urls) and will coordinate the call. Vanessa — can you confirm availability to execute the divert?

Rafael
Customer Escalations Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Mike O'Neil <ops@avalonhealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 08:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 502 spike and dropped throughput in us-west-2 (AZ2)

Rafael / Mike —

We're seeing the same signatures in our telemetry. I've kicked off a limited route reweight on the routing tier: 5% traffic to eu-west-1 for checkout, 0% to us-west-2a for new sessions, with sticky sessions honored for established connections. I pushed a quick KV-cache rebalance to reduce hot shard pressure (logs attached).

Attachments: kibana-az2-502-snippet.png, traffic-breakdown-20270707.csv

Observations so far:
- 502 spike aligns with a sudden heat in a small subset of cache keys (likely localized to hot paths from Avalon)
- Forwarding to eu-west-1 reduces 502 rate by ~70% on the canary route after 8 minutes

We can escalate to full drain of AZ2 for Avalon if you approve. This will impact latency for a subset of requests that prefer closest region; we recommend a coordinated one-hour maintenance window while we stabilize and then rehome traffic.

Vanessa
Routing Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Mike O'Neil <ops@avalonhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-lead@avalonhealth.com (Sofia Park)
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 502 spike and dropped throughput in us-west-2 (AZ2)

Thanks — the eu-west-1 canary reduced failures for test traffic. However, production users in the west are still seeing intermittent 502s when sessions route to us-west-2b. We need a deterministic mitigation and we also need an exec contact — our CISO and CTO are asking for an escalation path and potential credit if this keeps affecting payments.

Please confirm: if you activate a full regional drain for our tenant, how long to complete, and what is the expected impact on latency/throughput? Also share who from Redwood execs we can contact if we need a credit decision quickly.

Mike
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Mike O'Neil <ops@avalonhealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 502 spike and dropped throughput in us-west-2 (AZ2)

Mike / team —

Looping in Hannah (VP, Platform Ops) and Laura (Customer Success) for executive visibility and approvals. TL;DR proposed plan (approved by ops lead):
1) Immediate: full regional drain of Avalon traffic away from us-west-2a/b to us-west-2c + eu-west-1 for checkout routes; expected completion 12–20 minutes from approval. This is a soft drain (new sessions routed away; existing long-lived sessions honored for 10m) — should remove hot-KV pressure and reduce 502s substantially.
2) Mid: provision two emergency reserved inference nodes for Avalon (10–12 min) to relieve local node pressure and rehome shards.
3) Post-mortem: 72-hour retention of detailed request traces and increased token telemetry retention for Avalon (7 days) to support your compliance and audit needs.

Impacts & notes:
- Expected latency change: +30–80ms p95 for a small % of requests routed inter-region after drain; throughput should return to baseline once KV pressure is reduced.
- Credit/exec contact: Laura — please approve a one-time goodwill credit up to 30% of July usage for the time lost while we stabilize; Hannah please confirm the technical plan so we can proceed.
- Next: 9:00 PDT ops bridge (I'll schedule), we will send an official incident update to Avalon and their internal execs.

Attachments: proposed-evacuation-plan.pdf
Links: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/DL-AVALON-2026-09, https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-83421

Rafael
